Vinod Chandran, J. ===================== Vincent Mathew vs The Corporation Of Kochi on 22 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15592751/ 2 W.P.(C)Nos.13743 - P and 15413 of 2017 - B ========================= Dated this the 13th day of July, 2017 J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The issue raised in the above writ petition is with respect to a restaurant carried on in the name of New Malabar Restaurant in a property originally owned by one Jessy Joseph; in Survey No.95/17A comprised in Edapally North Village, in building No.49/1598 C. 2. W.P.(C) No.13743 of 2017 was filed by the petitioner therein seeking a direction to the Corporation to verify as to whether the 3rd respondent is carrying on the restaurant with a D&O license and license under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and if not to stop the restaurant forthwith. An interim order dated 28.04.2017 was passed directing verification of whether the 3rd respondent is carrying on the & 15413/2017 activity with proper permits and licenses from the respective statutory authorities. The 3rd respondent was then directed by the Corporation to stop the activity orally and the premises was locked and key taken over by the Corporation. The 3rd respondent challenged such action before this Court by W.P. (C) No.15413 of 2017, from which the documents and parties are referred to. 3. The petitioner commenced the hotel in the year 2013 and was also issued with D&O license which was renewed for the year 2014-2015. The petitioner had also been issued with a license under the Food Safety and Standards Act, which later was not renewed for reason of non renewal of D&O license. In fact the petitioner had approached this Court with a writ petition seeking direction to the Food Safety Authority to consider his application for renewal. Directions were also issued in W.P.(C) No.15494 of 2017, by judgment dated & 15413/2017 09.05.2017. To understand the dispute further, a brief statement of facts is required and essential. 4. The petitioner is said to have obtained lease of the building from one Ashraf, who was permitted to so lease out the building on the basis of an agreement for sale entered into with the owner of the property, one Jessy Joseph. The said Jessy Joseph is also said to have transferred the property to one Jose Thomas whose sister and Power of Attorney is impleaded as the additional 3rd respondent. The entire issue arose on the complaint raised by the additional 2nd respondent on an issue totally unconnected with the aforesaid transactions. The additional 2nd respondent is said to have taken food from the restaurant of the petitioner and developed some problems, based on which a complaint was raised before the Corporation to verify as to whether there was a license issued to the petitioner. & 15413/2017 5. The petitioner contends that the 2nd respondent is, in fact, a relative of the 3rd respondent and that the complaint was one initiated at the behest of the 3rd respondent. The learned Counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent however stoutly denies the same. This Court need not look into the same, since on the averments made by the 2nd respondent in the complaint and the writ petition Vincent Mathew vs The Corporation Of Kochi on 22 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15592751/ 3 filed by him, it is evident that the proceedings were initiated on the allegation of a food poisoning; which at any rate is a misplaced and misguided complaint. The 2nd respondent could have taken up appropriate proceedings on that allegation and the complaint on the question of licence was in fact unnecessary. 6. In any event, on that complaint the Corporation initiated proceedings and it was found that there was a dispute with respect to the possession and ownership of the property; which alone is germane for consideration in the writ petition. & 15413/2017 The Corporation had revoked the licence issued to the petitioner on such doubt raised as to the possession of the petitioner being not valid. The dispute was also on the ground that Jessy Joseph had in fact transferred the property to Jose Thomas and hence without a consent of Jose Thomas there could be no issuance of a D & O licence. 7. The revocation made by the Secretary was challenged before the Council, which rejected the appeal. The order in appeal was challenged before the Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions (Tribunal), which [LEAKAGE_MASK] the order at Ext.P3. On the aforesaid findings the Tribunal remanded the issue to the Secretary for re-consideration afresh by Ext.P3 order. It was & 15413/2017 specifically directed that the Secretary would look into whether Ashraf, who is said to have given possession of the property to the petitioner had obtained possession of the building prior to the sale deed in favour of the 3rd respondent. 8. After Ext.P3, the additional respondents impleaded before the Tribunal, ie; the additional respondents 2 and 3 filed a review which was rejected as per Ext.P4. The Secretary of the Corporation even after the remand did not make any consideration. This led to the closure of the petitioner's restaurant on the basis of the interim order in the other writ petition. & 15413/2017 9. As of now, it is admitted that the Corporation has not considered the issue and it is pending before the Secretary and is posted for hearing on 18.07.2017. It is found that Jessy Joseph on the very same day ie; on 23.09.2013 executed an agreement for sale in favour of Ashraf and also executed a sale deed in favour of Jose Thomas. Three suits are said to be pending, one filed by Ashraf, another filed by the petitioner and the third filed by Jose Joseph. Ashraf's suit is one for specific performance and setting aside the sale deed. The petitioner's suit is one for injunction, restraining the respondents from evicting the petitioner, unless in accordance with law.
texts.arguments: The leaned Counsel, who appears for the additional respondents 2 and 3 submits that Jessy Joseph was not even in India, when the said consent was issued, ie: on 21.11.2013, which consent is found to be in a non judicial stamp paper.
